{{Current events|year=2026|month=11|day=22|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Naval warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Naval warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Ukrainian attacks on the Russian shadow fleet]]
***Several people are killed and at least 10 others are injured after the [[Russian corvette Merkury|Russian corvette ''Merkury'']] is  struck by a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Unmanned surface vehicle|naval]] [[One-way attack drone|drone]] attack while docked at the port of [[Benghazi]], [[Libya]]. The ''Merkury'' later capsizes and sinks. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/11/22/suspected-drone-strike-hits-russian-vessel-in-libya (Al-Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/libyas-eastern-government-suspects-drone-attack-caused-explosion-russian-ship-2026-11-22/ (Reuters)]
***The ''M/V Angara'', a [[Russia|Russian]]-flagged cargo ship, is also struck by naval drones off the coast of Benghazi in the [[Mediterranean Sea]]. [https://www.npr.org/2026/11/23/g-s1-155017/ukraine-attack-russian-warship-libya (NPR)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**The ''[[Catholic World Report]]'' notes that at least 140 people were killed by [[Allied Democratic Forces]] and [[Islamic State Central Africa Province]] attacks targeting [[Christianity in the Democratic Republic of the Congo|Christians]] in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] [[Provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|provinces]] of [[North Kivu]] and [[Ituri Province|Ituri]] over the course of two weeks earlier in November. [https://www.catholicworldreport.com/2026/11/22/at-least-140-christians-killed-in-two-weeks-in-the-democratic-republic-of-congo/ (''Catholic World Report'')]
*[[South Sudanese Civil War]]
**Twenty-four people, including seven children, are killed in an attack by the armed wing of the [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement-in-Opposition]] in [[Tonj East County]], [[Warrap (state)|Warrap State]], [[South Sudan]]. Four attackers are also killed. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/24-civilians-killed-in-fresh-south-sudan-violence/ (CTV News)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**Two people are killed and thirteen others are abducted in two separate bandit attacks in [[Birnin Magaji/Kiyaw|Magaji]] and [[Maru, Nigeria|Maru]], [[Zamfara State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.tvcnews.tv/bandits-kill-two-teachers-abduct-13-in-zamfara-as-police-arrest-gunrunner-with-eight-ak-47-rifles/ (TVC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[63rd Golden Horse Awards]]
**The 63rd [[Golden Horse Awards]] take place in [[Taipei]], [[Taiwan]], with the [[Cinema of Hong Kong|Hong Kong film]] ''We Are Born Good'' winning [[Golden Horse Award for Best Narrative Feature|Best Narrative Feature]]. [https://www.afp.com/en/hong-kong-cinema-takes-spotlight-taiwan-top-film-award (AFP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests]]
**Several [[Textile industry in Bangladesh|garment factories]] in [[Gazipur]], [[Bangladesh]] declare holidays amid ongoing [[minimum wage]] protests, as clashes erupt between [[working class|workers]] and [[Bangladesh Police|police]] along the [[N3 (Bangladesh)|Dhaka–Mymensingh Highway]], with workers throwing bricks and police firing [[tear gas]] and [[stun grenade]]s while [[Special Response Battalion]], [[Bangladesh Ansar|Ansar]], [[Border Guard Bangladesh|BGB]], and [[Industrial Police (Bangladesh)|Industrial Police]] personnel deploy to the area. [https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/garment-workers-stage-fresh-protest-gazipur-attempt-block-dhaka-mymensingh-highway (''The Business Standard'')]
**[[Border Guard Bangladesh]] deploys 95 [[platoon]]s across seven districts, including two [[battalion]]s in [[Gopalganj District, Bangladesh|Gopalganj]], stepping up [[surveillance]] at key installations and industrial zones using [[unmanned aerial vehicle|drone]]s and [[police body camera]]s. [https://www.thedailystar.net/news/crime-justice/news/bgb-deploys-95-platoons-across-seven-districts-maintain-law-and-order-4330136 (''The Daily Star'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least twelve people are killed and 23 others are injured in two separate road accidents in [[Rajasthan]], [[India]]. [https://english.news.cn/20261122/a785c3b7251f4a10b97fb302966d242e/c.html (Xinhua)]
*A severe thunderstorm kills five people and injures more than 250 others in [[Tupanciretã]], [[Rio Grande do Sul]], [[Brazil]]. [https://www.afp.com/en/brazil-storm-death-toll-rises-5 (AFP)]
*Three people are killed in a house fire in [[Trzcianka]], [[Poland]]. [https://english.news.cn/20261122/bcadd59be9824a18b96cdca9f67305e5/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Carbon monoxide poisoning]] from a suspected [[heater]] malfunction during [[Sunday mass]] at a church in [[Bad Grönenbach]], [[Bavaria]], [[Germany]], leaves 56 people injured. [https://www.spiegel.de/panorama/bad-groenenbach-im-allgaeu-56-verletzte-bei-gottesdienst-wegen-kohlenmonoxid-austritt-a-ebf9cf29-ce27-49f4-8e74-e2d2756f9277 (''Der Spiegel'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference]]
**The 2026 [[United Nations Climate Change Conference]] (COP31) in [[Antalya]], [[Turkey]], concludes without a final agreement after countries failed to reach consensus on [[fossil fuel]] policies. It is the longest climate summit on record. [https://www.afp.com/en/climate-talks-collapse-chaotic-end-cop31 (AFP)] [https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/cop/cop31-climate-talks-close-final-deal-says-summit-president-2026-11-21/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Democratic Republic of the Congo–Kenya relations]]
**[[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] [[President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|president]] [[Félix Tshisekedi]] and [[Kenya]]n [[President of Kenya|president]] [[William Ruto]] agree to restore full [[diplomatic relations]] after a [[Summit (meeting)|summit]] in [[Oyo, Republic of the Congo]], hosted by the [[Republic of the Congo|country]]'s [[President of the Republic of the Congo|president]] [[Denis Sassou Nguesso]] and mediated by [[Togo]]lese former [[President of Togo|president]] [[Faure Gnassingbé]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmvg2qnn95vro (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[Co-op Live]] arena in [[Manchester]], [[England]], is evacuated of around 12000 attendees after an unknown substance is dispersed during a [[Don Toliver]] concert, initially believed to be [[tear gas]], causing respiratory distress to multiple concertgoers. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9e851dn8516o (BBC News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/11/23/europe/manchester-coop-live-tear-gas-don-toliver-hnk-intl (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[South Korea]]n [[Minister of Education (South Korea)|education minister]] [[Choi Kyo-jin]] resigns following criticism of [[Government of South Korea|the government]]'s response to [[artificial intelligence]]-assisted cheating concerns surrounding the [[College Scholastic Ability Test]]. [[President of South Korea|President]] [[Lee Jae Myung]] accepts Choi's resignation. [https://www.afp.com/en/south-korea-education-chief-resigns-amid-ai-cheating-scandal (AFP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 ATP Finals]]
**In [[tennis]], [[Carlos Alcaraz]] defeats [[Alexander Zverev]] 6–2, 7–6<sup>(9–7)</sup> in the final to win his first [[Singles (tennis)|singles]] title at the 2026 [[ATP Finals]]. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/tennis/alcaraz-charges-past-world-number-one-zverev-clinch-atp-finals-title-2026-11-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 MotoGP World Championship]]
**In [[motorcycle racing]], [[Spain|Spanish]] rider [[Marc Márquez]] of [[Ducati Corse]] secures his eighth [[MotoGP World Championship]] after finishing eighth at the [[2026 Portuguese motorcycle Grand Prix|Portuguese Grand Prix]], equalling [[Giacomo Agostini]]'s [[List of Grand Prix motorcycle racing rider records|record]] for the most premier-class motorcycle racing world titles. [https://apnews.com/article/marc-marquez-motogp-99638bd5dcc6a86106edba209851ad8f (AP)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=11|day=23|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Ukraine]] launches a large-scale [[Drone warfare|drone attack]] across [[European Russia|western Russia]], striking the [[Perm refinery]] in [[Perm Krai]] and [[Novoshakhtinsk]] refinery in [[Rostov Oblast]]. [https://kyivindependent.com/novoshakhtinsk-oil-refinery-reportedly-burning-after-ukrainian-drone-attack/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')] [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/23/ukrainian-drones-kill-1-strike-oil-refinery-in-perm-region-a94347 (''The Moscow Times'')]
*[[Kurdish–Turkish conflict]]
**[[Turkey|Turkish]] [[National Intelligence Organization|intelligence]] reports that the [[Kurdistan Workers' Party]] withdraws from 14 additional bases in [[Iraqi Kurdistan|northern Iraq]] as part of an ongoing [[disarmament]] process aimed at ending its conflict with [[Turkey]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20261123-turkey-says-pkk-evacuated-14-more-bases-in-northern-iraq (AFP via France 24)]
*At least 15 people are injured and 28 houses and shops are [[vandalism|vandalised]] during clashes between rival [[Bangladesh Nationalist Party]] factions in [[Shailkupa Upazila]], [[Jhenaidah District]], [[Bangladesh]]. [https://www.thedailystar.net/news/crime-justice/news/15-injured-bnp-factions-clash-jhenaidah-4331446 (''The Daily Star'')]
*At least 20 people are injured, five seriously, and several shops are [[vandalism|vandalised]] as rival factions of the banned [[Awami League]] clash and detonate four [[improvised explosive device|crude bomb]]s in [[Gopalganj Sadar Upazila]], [[Gopalganj District, Bangladesh|Gopalganj District]], [[Bangladesh]]. [https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/least-20-injured-clash-between-two-al-factions-gopalganj-1612076 (''The Business Standard'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Jensen Huang scandal]], [[Chinese intelligence activity abroad]]
**[[Nvidia]] reinstates [[Jensen Huang]] as [[president (corporate title)|president]] and [[chief executive officer]] less than two weeks after he resigned following revelations of an [[affair]] with [[Alice Huang (executive)|Alice Huang]], who is suspected by [[United States Intelligence Community|U.S. intelligence]] of [[espionage|spying]] for [[China]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-reinstates-jensen-huang-ceo/ (CBS)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Seven people are killed and two others are injured after a truck loaded with stones overturns onto a minitruck in [[Punjab, Pakistan]]. [https://english.news.cn/20261123/00ed81bb7e0043e5a18f3db0c2170696/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Tajikistan]] formally begins the process of withdrawing from the [[International Criminal Court]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/tajikistan-becomes-fourth-country-withdraw-icc-since-us-diplomatic-push-2026-11-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**The [[Supreme Court of Spain|Supreme Court]] of [[Spain]] grants [[amnesty]] to former [[President of Catalonia|Catalan president]] [[Carles Puigdemont]], who is currently in self-imposed [[exile]] in [[Belgium]], thereby bringing the legal proceedings against the leaders of the [[Catalan declaration of independence|October 2017 declaration of independence]] to a definitive close. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/11/23/europe/spanish-court-carles-puigdemont-exile-intl (CNN)]
*[[2026 European bomb threat wave]]
**Hundreds of schools across [[Denmark]] and [[Germany]] receive [[bomb threat]]s via [[email]], with police ordering the schools to continue operations as normal. [https://www.reuters.com/world/hundreds-german-schools-received-bomb-threats-bild-reports-2026-11-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 European unrest]]
**A 58-year-old student dies at [[Sapienza University of Rome|Sapienza University]] in [[Rome]], [[Italy]], while being on a [[hunger strike]] protesting the fact that he had not been assigned a place to stay. [https://www.fanpage.it/roma/studente-muore-in-tenda-alla-sapienza-cardiopatico-era-in-attesa-di-un-alloggio-nello-studentato/ (Fanpage {{small|in Italian}})]
*[[Hijab in Iran]]
**[[Iran]]ian singer [[Parastoo Ahmadi]] receives 74 [[Flagellation|lashes]] for performing at a music concert without a hijab. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cq1j6585l5g6o (BBC)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup bids]]
**In [[association football]], [[FIFA]] confirms [[Costa Rican Football Federation|Costa Rica]], [[Jamaica Football Federation|Jamaica]], [[Mexican Football Federation|Mexico]], and the [[United States Soccer Federation|United States]] as joint hosts of the [[2031 FIFA Women's World Cup|2031 Women's World Cup]], while [[The Football Association|England]], [[Irish Football Association|Northern Ireland]], [[Scottish Football Association|Scotland]], and [[Football Association of Wales|Wales]] will jointly host the [[2035 FIFA Women's World Cup|2035 tournament]]. [https://www.afp.com/en/usa-joint-bid-host-2031-womens-world-cup-uk-host-2035 (AFP)]
